subject: Intermittent 502s — SNAT port reuse, PMTUD blackholes, and SG audit for private deployment
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@northbridge.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
Cc: ops@northbridge.io
Date: Sat, 6 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: [NorthBridge] Intermittent 502s from on-prem agents to Redwood Private

Hi Priyom —

We're seeing sporadic 502s from our on-prem agents when they call the private endpoint (private.redwood-nb.local). Problem started yesterday afternoon after a firewall firmware upgrade. Symptoms:
- ~1-2% of requests fail with 502, client TCP shows reset from server side.
- Failures cluster on long-poll (60s) connections and large payload uploads (15-30MB).
- Traceroutes from agent to edge show no path change; capture attached.

We've attached a pcap and a snippet of our security group rules. Can you confirm if this looks like NAT port exhaustion, MTU fragmentation, or a security group rule blocking ICMP/PATH MTU? We're running the private deployment in our VPC with the dedicated Private box you provisioned.

Thanks,
Carlos Vega
NetOps Manager
NorthBridge Medical Systems

Attachments: vpn-trace-20270206.pcap, sg-config-snippet.txt

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.example>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@northbridge.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 6 Feb 2027 10:08:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: [NorthBridge] Intermittent 502s from on-prem agents to Redwood Private

Carlos —

Thanks for the packet capture and SG snippet. Quick read shows:
- Repeated SYN/ACKs followed by RSTs for long-lived connections (likely server side tear-down).
- Several "Fragmentation needed but DF set" ICMPs are visible but dropped intermittently before reaching the agent's IP.
- TCP segments in the pcap sometimes exceed the MTU on intermediate link (we saw 9198B frames intermittently).

A few hypotheses:
1) PMTUD is failing because intermediate firewall is blocking ICMP type 3/code 4; large packets are being blackholed.
2) Edge SNAT port reuse + many ephemeral connections (long-poll) is causing conntrack collisions and unexpected RST behavior.
3) NIC offloading (TSO/LRO) + firewall fragment handling mismatch is showing larger frames to capture tools and confusing path behaviour.

I'll loop in Rishi and Dev to propose immediate mitigations and a short-term rollback plan. Can you confirm a maintenance window tomorrow morning (2/7) to test a couple of quick changes?

–Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>

Date: Sat, 6 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: [NorthBridge] Intermittent 502s from on-prem agents to Redwood Private

Folks —

I dug into our edge box telemetry for your tenant. Observations:
- High number of TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED sockets mapped to a small ephemeral port range. SNAT is done at our LB and at your firewall (double NAT).
- conntrack shows many short-lived entries followed by immediate terminates; nf_conntrack_max on your border FW is set low (50k).

Immediate mitigation steps (low risk):
- On your firewall: increase nf_conntrack_max to 200k and tune nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established to 86400 for long poll sockets.
- On the edge host: temporarily disable TSO/LRO on the uplink interface to avoid oversized segments being emitted. Command: ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
- Allow ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed) between the path MTU-affecting devices and the agent subnets.

If you want me to run these during your window tomorrow, I can prepare step-by-step commands. Also attaching conntrack-stats.log for reference.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: [NorthBridge] Intermittent 502s from on-prem agents to Redwood Private

Hi all —

Thanks, Dev. Two additional notes from the runtime side:
- We can enable explicit SNAT port reuse on the edge LB (reuseport-like behavior) to reduce ephemeral consumption. That requires a brief restart of the LB service (estimated 90s).
- For a safer rollback, we'll first push the firewall conntrack tunings on your side and monitor for an hour before touching LB config.

Proposed runbook for 02/07 09:30-10:30 EST (needs your sign-off):
1) 09:30: Disable TSO/LRO on edge uplink (Dev) + enable conntrack tuning on NB firewall (NB Ops)
2) 09:45: Monitor metrics (502 rate, conntrack usage, ephemeral ports) for 20m
3) 10:05: If stable, enable SNAT port reuse on LB and roll for 2 canaries (90s window)
4) 10:20: Re-enable offloads if no regressions, else rollback changes

Carlos — can you confirm NB Ops can do step 1 at 09:30? Also please share a preferred Slack/phone bridge.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Networking
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 7 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: [NorthBridge] Intermittent 502s from on-prem agents to Redwood Private — Runbook confirmed

Carlos / NB Ops —

Thanks for confirming the maintenance window. We ran the agreed steps at 09:30:
- NB applied conntrack tunings (nf_conntrack_max=200000; tcp timeout updated).
- Dev disabled TSO/LRO on the uplink for 30m during tests.
- Rishi toggled SNAT port reuse on two LB canaries (90s restart each).

Outcome summary:
- 502 rate dropped from ~1.8% to 0.05% within 15 minutes of the conntrack increase.
- PMTUD ICMPs stopped being dropped after the firewall rule change; large uploads completed without fragmentation errors.
- No immediate side effects observed from disabling offloads; we re-enabled them after a 30m soak.

Follow-ups (action items):
- NB: make conntrack tunings permanent and document in change control (Carlos).
- Redwood: we'll add a short KB on recommended firewall/ICMP rules and a pre-deploy checklist for PMTUD friendliness (Priyom).
- Both: schedule a 1-hour network posture review next week to avoid surprises when firewall firmwares change.

If you want us to close the ticket, reply-all with a quick "ack".

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference
